description: minimumReleaseAge holds every version bump for 3 days. Automerge reaches containers that are root-equivalent on every fleet host (see the cadvisor/node_exporter rule below), and gitops_reconcile applies a merge within ~15 min, so a version published an hour ago could otherwise be live in one cycle with no human in the loop. Three days is the window in which a compromised or broken release is normally yanked. It reaches neither digest updates nor container images at all — see the two rules below.

Two defaults make this cheap rather than costly, both checked against the pinned renovate: internalChecksFilter is strict, so a too-young version opens no PR at all instead of a pending one; and vulnerabilityAlerts sets minimumReleaseAge to null with prCreation immediate, so an OSV fix still lands the moment it exists.

customManagers.description: Container image refs pinned in role vars; quadlet templates render them.

The disaster-recovery runbook hardcodes the wordpress-db mariadb image so its fallback SQL load runs on the engine the role pins; same depName as roles/wordpress/vars wordpress_db_image, so renovate bumps the runbook copy in the same PR.
Grafana dashboard revisions pinned in role vars; the role fetches them from grafana.com at converge.

tflint pinned for CI (the lint workflow's setup-tflint) and the workstation (roles/dev/vars); no zypper package. Same depName, so both bump together; the pattern matches tflint_version and dev_tflint_version.

OpenTofu pinned for CI in both workflows' setup-opentofu step (lint.yml and terraform.yml); no zypper package renovate can track, so it follows upstream releases. Same depName, so both bump together; the terraform workflow's destructive-plan gate guards the live apply a terraform.yml bump fires, so minor/patch automerge like any other bump.
Hugo pinned in the Firebase deploy workflows and the go.sum autofix workflow (peaceiris/actions-hugo hugo-version); no zypper/pip package.
firebase-tools pinned in the Firebase deploy workflows (npx firebase-tools@<version>); the CLI does the keyless deploy.

The ansible MCP server pinned in .mcp.json (npx @ansible/ansible-mcp-server@<version>); no pip/zypper package, so it follows the npm release like firebase-tools, alongside the ansible-lint/molecule pins in requirements-dev.txt.

terraform/main.tf's required_version constrains the OpenTofu CLI, but renovate's terraform manager tracks it as hashicorp/terraform (disabled in a packageRule below). Track it against opentofu/opentofu instead, matching the tofu_version CI pin; hashicorp versioning parses the ~> range.

packageRules.description: Grafana dashboard revisions are bare incrementing integers.
pinDigest updates carry no version change, so the lint check is enough to merge them unattended.

minimumReleaseAge cannot gate a digest update: renovate reads no releaseTimestamp for a docker digest (renovatebot/renovate#38656), the lookup pushes digest updates past the internalChecksFilter entirely, and minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour defaults to timestamp-required — so the branch worker marks every digest bump pending on a renovate/stability-days check that no elapsed time can clear, and none of them ever automerge. Clearing minimumReleaseAge skips that check, since the branch worker only runs it for a non-empty value. pinDigest is included because a newly added image pins the same way. This sets no automerge, so the rule below still holds cadvisor and caddy back for a human.

No registry renovate reads here returns a releaseTimestamp for an image: measured across all 22 pinned images, not one carries one, while every terraform and gomod dep does. Under the timestamp-required default that parks a container version bump on the same permanently-pending check, so the window has never actually gated a container — redis 8.8.1 merged five hours after it was published. Clearing minimumReleaseAge states that plainly instead of leaving bumps stuck behind a check that never resolves. The rule above still covers digest updates on the other datasources, which is where the github-actions pins live.

No unattended bump where a compromised image reads the host or fronts the internet. cadvisor runs as root with a read-only bind of the entire host filesystem, so an image compromise reads every secret on the host — measured: it reads a mode-0600 root-owned file, cannot write, and holds no capability. caddy terminates TLS for the public sites, holds the Cloudflare API token, and is the only container publishing 80/443. node_exporter is deliberately NOT here: it mounts the host D-Bus system bus, but the upstream image runs it as an unprivileged uid, so systemd refuses it StartTransientUnit, and its molecule verify now asserts that user — the one image change that would make the mount dangerous fails the tier before automerge can reach it. Must stay after the pinDigest rule above: later rules win. A packageRule is the right shape even though :automergeMinor and :automergeDigest set automerge through update-type objects instead — flatten applies packageRules once more after merging those, so this still has the last word.

requirements.txt pins the ansible that gitops_reconcile installs into its venv and then applies the whole fleet with, as root — so an unattended bump is new root-privileged code on every host that nobody read. Hashing the pin would not help: the apply is root from the fetched tree either way, and pip's hash mode is per-invocation, so it would force a pinned, hashed transitive closure onto requirements-dev.txt as well (CI, the Makefile, bootstrap/incus.yml and roles/dev all install through it). Requiring a human read is the control that fits.
linuxserver images carry legacy build-number (151), two-part (5.14), and four-part tags that docker versioning reads as upgrades; their releases are strict semver, so reject the rest.
lidarr has a legacy 8.1.2135 tag that even strict semver accepts; mainline is 3.x.
Merging a plex bump deploys a container restart that kills active streams; only automerge in the small hours.

python-dateutil is a hard dep of hetzner.hcloud (its vendored hcloud SDK imports dateutil.parser.isoparse); upstream tried datetime.fromisoformat and reverted over the ISO-8601 Z suffix. It's stable, not abandoned, just release-inactive.

Blowfish (the Hugo theme) is an indirect gomod require in jonnyoc-site; config:best-practices skips indirect gomod deps, so enable them for that go.mod or the theme never updates. Minor/patch automerge like hugo: site-gate catches a build/compat break, and hugo-gosum-autofix.yml completes go.sum and re-triggers the gate on its amended commit.

required_version in terraform/main.tf constrains the OpenTofu CLI, not HashiCorp Terraform; the terraform manager mis-tracks it as hashicorp/terraform. Disable that — the custom manager above tracks it as opentofu/opentofu.
